note: Re-quoted 2026-11-25 to the Open Word Bible (OWB), Amharic, Balanced edition (CC0; library/data/bible/owb-am-b.json.gz, read offline as owb-am), per the founder decision of 2026-11-18 (Amharic quotes OWB everywhere). This supersedes what the notes below say about the 1962 UBS Bible and about wording borrowed from other Amharic works: every `mined` row is now a verbatim OWB span in its block (exact OWB pieces may be joined with '…'); `self_rendered` rows are allusions and paraphrases left as the translator's prose.

Isaiah 45:22: the verse itself is OWB (blocks 5 and 18; the 'modern translation' of block 18 now reads the same OWB words). Spurgeon heard the KJV 'Look unto me', and the chapter turns on 'look', so block 5 adds a one-time bridge after the verse («ዞር በሉ» read «ተመልከቱ» in that translation) and the refrain «ወደ እኔ ተመልከቱ» (blocks 5, 15 heading, 16) stays the word he heard — the Spurgeon bio's bridge, reused. The book row's about_html quotes the series verse 1 Timothy 4:12 as OWB «ወጣት በመሆንህ ማንም አይናቅህ»; series.json's am verse_text should match it.

Scripture authority is the 1962 Amharic Bible (UBS; NT revised 2003), the text the shipped Amharic house books quote. Its New Testament is on disk whole (ebible mirror, bibles/amh_amh via scripts/bible_mirror.py); the mirror carries no Old Testament, so OT quotations reuse the wording of an already-shipped Amharic work where one quotes the same verse (source_file names it) and are otherwise self_rendered in the 1962 register.

The English quotes the BSB, except where a story gives the words a person heard (Spurgeon's KJV Isaiah 45:22). The Amharic keeps the 1962 wording throughout; Isaiah 45:22 uses the shipped cheque-book.am.json form with ተመልከቱ ('look'), which the chapter's whole point turns on. The 1962 printed text reads ወደ እኔ ዘወር በሉ (as talks-to-the-farmer.am.json quotes it) — a native reviewer should confirm the 'look' form. The chapter's second, 'modern translation' rendering of the verse is self_rendered and deliberately different.

1 Timothy 4:12 is inside a bridged 4:11-13 entry in the mirror and has no shipped Amharic rendering, so it is self_rendered. Daniel 5:27 reuses Richard Allen's own Amharic edition (ጐድለህም); the 1962 Bible reads ቀልለህም.
A mined row was checked as an exact substring of the cited source (1962 NT verse or corpus file) inside the named block.
